  • 𝒩\mathcal{N} the normalization of a Clebsch–Gordan or subduction block ℰ/𝒩\mathcal{E}/\sqrt{\mathcal{N}}
  • ∣ μΓ;κ⟩\bigl\lvert{}^{\Gamma}_{\,\mu};\kappa\bigr\rangle the partner μ\mu of the copy κ\kappa of the irrep Γ\Gamma in a product, or of Λ\Lambda in a restriction
  • ∣ μΓ⟩\bigl\lvert{}^{\Gamma}_{\,\mu}\bigr\rangle the partner μ\mu of the irrep Γ\Gamma, a vector of its basis
  • ⟨ μ1Γ1  μ2Γ2∣ μΓ;κ⟩\bigl\langle{}^{\Gamma_1}_{\,\mu_1}\,{}^{\Gamma_2}_{\,\mu_2}\bigm\vert{}^{\Gamma}_{\,\mu};\kappa\bigr\rangle the Clebsch–Gordan coefficient of a finite group in Γ1⊗Γ2→Γ\Gamma_1 \otimes \Gamma_2 \to \Gamma, for the copy κ\kappa of Γ\Gamma
  • μ1,μ2\mu_1, \mu_2 the partners of the two factors of a product

Encodings
TeX \bigl\lvert{}^{\Gamma}_{\,\mu};\kappa\bigr\rangle = \sum_{\mu_1,\mu_2}\bigl\langle{}^{\Gamma_1}_{\,\mu_1}\,{}^{\Gamma_2}_{\,\mu_2}\bigm\vert{}^{\Gamma}_{\,\mu};\kappa\bigr\rangle\;\bigl\lvert{}^{\Gamma_1}_{\,\mu_1}\bigr\rangle\bigl\lvert{}^{\Gamma_2}_{\,\mu_2}\bigr\rangle,

where μ1\mu_1, μ2\mu_2 and μ\mu are counted from 1. Each block is headed Γ1⊗Γ2→Γ\Gamma_1\otimes\Gamma_2\to\Gamma, κ\kappa (trivial when Γ\Gamma occurs once in Γ1⊗Γ2\Gamma_1\otimes\Gamma_2) and a normalization 𝒩\mathcal{N}. Row μ\mu gives the nonzero terms of 𝒩 ∣ μΓ;κ⟩\sqrt{\mathcal{N}}\,\bigl\lvert{}^{\Gamma}_{\,\mu};\kappa\bigr\rangle, each coefficient times 𝒩\sqrt{\mathcal{N}}, with ∣μ1 μ2⟩\lvert {\mu_1}\,{\mu_2}\rangle for ∣ μ1Γ1⟩∣ μ2Γ2⟩\bigl\lvert{}^{\Gamma_1}_{\,\mu_1}\bigr\rangle\bigl\lvert{}^{\Gamma_2}_{\,\mu_2}\bigr\rangle, so that the squared moduli of a row sum to 𝒩\mathcal{N}. Only Γ1≤Γ2\Gamma_1 \le \Gamma_2 is listed (Γ2⊗Γ1\Gamma_2\otimes\Gamma_1 exchanges μ1\mu_1 and μ2\mu_2), and a block whose two factors are one-dimensional is left out: it is ∣Γ⟩=∣Γ1⟩∣Γ2⟩\lvert \Gamma\rangle = \lvert \Gamma_1\rangle\lvert \Gamma_2\rangle, ⟨Γ1 Γ2∣Γ⟩=1\langle \Gamma_1\,\Gamma_2\mid \Gamma\rangle = 1. Where Γ\Gamma occurs more than once, κ\kappa is followed by the rule that separates its copies (Conventions, section 10.4). The copies labeled exch. sym. and exch. anti. are symmetric and antisymmetric under the exchange of the two factors. The copies labeled cross. sym. and cross. anti. are symmetric and antisymmetric under the crossing. The copies labeled lowest parent and complement are the copy that the rule of 𝖲𝖮(𝟥)\mathsf{SO(3)} parentage selects and its orthogonal complement.
